# Temple Scroll Column 50 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 50 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**50:1** If a man has two wives, the one loved and the other hated, and they bear him sons — both the loved and the hated —

**50:2** and the firstborn son belongs to the hated wife —

**50:3** then on the day he gives as an inheritance to his sons what he has, he shall not treat the son of the loved as the firstborn in place of the son of the hated, who is the firstborn.

**50:4** But he shall acknowledge the son of the hated as the firstborn, by giving him a double portion of all that he has; for he is the first of his strength, and the right of the firstborn is his.

**50:5** If a man has two wives, the one loved and the other hated, and they bear him sons, both the loved and the hated — he shall not exchange the birthright.

**50:6** And the firstborn son is the son of the hated — he shall not treat the son of the loved as firstborn in place of the son of the hated who is the firstborn.

**50:7** For the right of the firstborn belongs to the son of the hated wife; he is the first of his strength.

**50:8** If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not obey the voice of his father or the voice of his mother —

**50:9** and they discipline him, and he does not listen to them —

**50:10** then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place.

**50:11** If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not obey the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and they discipline him, and he does not listen to them —

**50:12** then his father and his mother shall say to the elders of his city: This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he does not obey our voice; he is a glutton and a drunkard.

**50:13** And all the men of his city shall stone him with stones, and he shall die; and you shall purge the evil from your midst, and all Israel shall hear and be afraid.

**50:14** And if a man has committed a sin worthy of death and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree —

**50:15** his body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but you shall surely bury him on that day; for a hanged man is a curse of God, and you shall not defile your land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance.

**50:16** You shall not see the ox of your brother or his sheep going astray and hide yourself from them; you shall surely bring them back to your brother.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows EMET throughout. "Hated" retained for senuah (vv. 1-7) over LOGOS's "unloved" — the Hebrew senuah is strong language that the text does not soften. "Hang on a tree" preserved (v. 14) over LOGOS's "impale on a stake" — "tree" for etz is the traditional and literal rendering with deep theological resonance (cf. Galatians 3:13, Acts 5:30). "Curse of God" preserved for qilelat elohim — the deliberate ambiguity (cursed by God? an affront to God?) is part of the text's meaning. "Glutton and drunkard" retained over LOGOS's "profligate" and PNEUMA's "wastrel."*
